titleFront: Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi
titleBack: Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe

flipToBack.prose: Flip if Vader can be spotted at a battleground site AND no opponent Jedi or Luke can be spotted at a battleground site. Both spots use SpotOverride.INCLUDE_EXCLUDED_FROM_BATTLE. Note: this is canSpot ('at'), NOT control or occupy.

children.req: card-spot: Vader at a battleground site (presence at location, ownership of location irrelevant)
card-spot: any opponent Jedi or Luke at a battleground site
children.gameConditions: GameConditions.canSpot(game, self, SpotOverride.INCLUDE_EXCLUDED_FROM_BATTLE, Filters.and(Filters.opponents(self), Filters.or(Filters.Jedi, Filters.Luke), Filters.at(Filters.battleground_site)))

flipToFront.prose: Back flips to front if opponent has a Jedi or Luke at a battleground site, OR Vader cannot be spotted on table. SpotOverride.INCLUDE_EXCLUDED_FROM_BATTLE.

children.req: card-spot: opponent Jedi or Luke at a battleground site
children.gameConditions: GameConditions.canSpot(game, self, SpotOverride.INCLUDE_EXCLUDED_FROM_BATTLE, Filters.and(Filters.opponents(self), Filters.or(Filters.Jedi, Filters.Luke), Filters.at(Filters.battleground_site)))

requirementSemantics: flipToBack: pure canSpot presence semantics ('with actor at location-type'), no control/occupy anywhere. Vader must be AT a battleground site; site need not be controlled or even occupied in force.
flipToBack negative leaf: canSpot of opponent Jedi-or-Luke at ANY battleground site blocks the flip (global, not same-site).
flipToFront: disjunction. Either opponent gets Jedi/Luke to a battleground site (canSpot), or Vader leaves the table (NOT canSpot Vader).
All spots use SpotOverride.INCLUDE_EXCLUDED_FROM_BATTLE, so battle-excluded cards still count.
NOTE vs 213_31: this Special Edition version checks Filters.or(Filters.Jedi, Filters.Luke); it does NOT include padawans.
typedIdentities: Filters.battleground_site (flip gate location type on both sides)
Filters.and(Filters.opponents(self), Filters.or(Filters.Jedi, Filters.Luke), Filters.at(Filters.battleground_site)) (flip blocker / flip-back trigger)

Back: Filters.sameLocationAs(self, Filters.and(Filters.opponents(self), Filters.or(Filters.Jedi, Filters.Skywalker))) (no battle/drain lock); Filters.Meditation_Chamber + Filters.Vader (battle destiny -2); Filters.or(Filters.Sense, Filters.Alter) (opponent may not play)

seedMismatches: Seed flipRequirements labels the relation PRESENT with byWhom Vader at battleground_site; source is GameConditions.canSpot of Filters.and(Filters.Vader, Filters.at(Filters.battleground_site))). Semantically 'at', not 'present at' in the SWCCG presence sense; minor terminology drift, same practical meaning here.
Seed omits the SpotOverride.INCLUDE_EXCLUDED_FROM_BATTLE detail on both flip directions (the K2 seed records it only for 213_31).

profile.frontStructuredRule: preFlip/flip allOf: any Vader at a runtime battleground site in rules terms, and zero opponent Jedi-or-Luke at any runtime battleground site in rules terms; include excluded-from-battle cards
profile.backStructuredRule: postFlip/flipBack anyOf: zero Vader on table, or opponent Jedi-or-Luke at a runtime battleground site in rules terms; include excluded-from-battle cards
profileGaps: The three place-out-of-play predicates remain source-owned rather than duplicated in objective data. ObjectiveHardLossPolicy now guards Scanning Crew, non-Epic duel initiation, and Executor-site Force drains only while classic Hunt Down is active.
The four-Force recall remains engine game text. AI policy scores its exact live source and binds the physical Vader target while preserving a sole required Vader.

missingStateCalculation: Front is complete only when a real Vader persona is at a runtime battleground site and no opponent Jedi or Luke is at any runtime battleground site. The battleground need not be controlled, and opponent-owned Vader also satisfies the source's unscoped actor spot.
A Padawan who is neither a Jedi nor Luke is not a classic blocker. A blocker at a non-battleground is irrelevant. A title containing Vader without Persona.VADER is not the actor.

After flip, Vader may leave the battleground and remain anywhere on table without causing flip-back. The missing state begins only when no Vader remains on table or a classic blocker reaches any battleground.
flipPreservation: Before flip, deploy and movement doctrine favor a legal runtime battleground destination for the last needed Vader. Landspeed and the complete docking-bay transit parent/destination/mover chain use exact legal routes. They do not require a buddy or friendly control.
Force-loss and battle-forfeit selection preserve the last needed Vader only when another legal loss exists. Unavoidable loss remains selectable.

After flip, the last Vader anywhere on table is protected from avoidable forfeit. Movement from a battleground to Vader's Castle is not blocked because battleground presence is no longer the stay-flipped law.
Safe battle scoring targets a remote Jedi-or-Luke blocker. Formation Safety, predictor defeat, effective power below the established boundary, low Reserve, and V25 anti-suicide remain absolute.
runtimeOwners: ObjectiveAnalyzer.assessFlipLocationRules owns the classic allOf front law and anyOf back law with runtime battleground, controller-any actor, opponent blocker, and on-table semantics.

ObjectiveAnalyzer.classifyPreFlipProgressCandidate, getDeployObjectiveAdjustments, advancesPreFlipActorAtRuntimeLocation, and wouldCompletePreFlipRequirementAt own Vader pull, parent deploy, destination deploy, movement, and exact completion facts.
DeployTacticalPolicy V51 now receives a complete-objective fact instead of an opponent-site guess. It scores only when every live classic condition is true.
MoveDestinationPolicy owns the +600 legal actor-location start and +1000 legal advancing destination contributions after both Formation Safety vetoes.
ObjectiveBattlePolicy BATTLE.OBJECTIVE.GLOBAL_BLOCKER_REMOVAL owns the bounded safe battle against a remote classic blocker.
ForceLossPolicy V21-objective and BattleForfeitPolicy BATTLE.OBJECTIVE.FLIP_GATE_FORMATION_HOLD preserve the required pre-flip or last on-table Vader.
ObjectiveHardLossPolicy owns classic-only Scanning Crew, non-Epic duel, and Executor-site drain vetoes. ObjectiveAnalyzer resets identity when the objective leaves play so these guards cannot leak.
ObjectiveAnalyzer and the mirrored Combined, Move, and CardSelection evaluators own docking-bay transit source, exact destination, and mover binding across the engine's cancel-suffixed prompts.
Rando and Chosen One adapters call the same shared analyzers and policies.
contradictions: Printed Force icons are not runtime battleground truth. Every deploy and movement decision reads Filters.battleground_site through the live modifier query.
The actor controller is any, not self. The blocker controller is opponent. The source does not require Dark Side control of Vader's site.
Classic Hunt Down excludes Padawan from its blocker filter. The virtual profile includes Padawan and is tested separately.
Pre-flip requires Vader at a battleground. Post-flip requires Vader only somewhere on table. Reusing the front location hold after flip would be false.
Vader is the complete count-one formation for this law. A generic buddy requirement would invent card text.
